claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC alloy.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy was prepared by vacuum arc melting and annealed at approximately 1300 °C.
TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
A controlled minor oxygen addition during melting or post-melt annealing is proposed for TiVNbTa.
Controlled oxygen addition and heat treatment will form TiO precipitates within the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
The TiO precipitates will be nanoscale and uniformly dispersed.
The TiO precipitates will be coherent or semi-coherent with the BCC matrix.
Heat treatment at 1200–1300 °C for several hours under controlled oxygen partial pressure will enable TiO nucleation and growth.
Rapid cooling after oxygen-assisted heat treatment will preserve the desired TiO precipitate distribution.
TiO precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
The proposed precipitation-strengthening effect will remain effective at 1273 K despite thermally activated dislocation glide.
Mechanical alloying and spark-plasma sintering of NbMoTaWVTi produced a BCC matrix containing an FCC TiO precipitated phase.
The TiO-containing NbMoTaWVTi alloy had substantially higher compressive strength than an as-cast counterpart, with the improvement attributed to grain refinement and precipitation strengthening.
The oxygen-modified TiVNbTa alloy will have markedly higher yield strength than the 330 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The 1273 K yield strength could potentially double relative to the 330 MPa baseline.
The strengthened alloy will retain acceptable ductility for use as a W-to-CuCrZr interlayer.
Inert or vacuum testing near 1273 K under tensile or compressive loading represents the intended interlayer service environment.
Oxygen modification may adversely affect ductility, thermal conductivity, or oxidation resistance.
